issues.body: EntityLinker::link calls exact_iri_entities unconditionally. Consequently EntityLinker::build(...).link(...) and NlqConfig { link_entities: true, link_values: false, ... } now link verbatim IRIs, despite the README, NlqConfig documentation, and skill describing both exact-dictionary probes as part of link_values and saying that setting is off by default. The new unlabelled_entity_still_links_by_verbatim_iri test confirms this unintended default-on behavior by omitting with_values(). This can alter prompts and invalidate recorded fixtures for users who enabled the pre-existing entity linker but did not opt into the new tier.
issues.fix_hint: Gate exact_iri_entities behind the same opt-in state as literal values (for example, store an explicit values/dictionary-linking enabled flag set by with_values), and update the verbatim-IRI tests to require with_values(). Add a regression test proving that a verbatim IRI does not link when the exact dictionary tier is disabled. Alternatively, if default-on IRI probing is intentional, revise all public docs/config semantics and explicitly account for the backward-compatible prompt/fixture impact.
issues.title: Verbatim IRI linking bypasses the link_values opt-in

verdict.summary: The literal-value index is plausibly implemented and its datatype/language preservation tests exercise the real linker path, but the verbatim-IRI behavior is not actually gated by the new opt-in setting. This contradicts the public configuration contract and changes existing entity-linking behavior whenever link_entities is enabled, even though link_values remains false.
